logo.description: URL or relative path to provider logo

abstract.description: Short description of what the provider offers

access.description: free = no auth needed; api-key = free with key; paid = commercial; registration = free after sign-up

apiKeyUrl.description: Where to obtain an API key

setupUrl.description: Setup or dashboard URL for domain/property registration

note.description: Free-text setup note shown in the UI, e.g. authentication instructions

license.description: Data license, e.g. ODbL, CC-BY-4.0, proprietary

status.description: DEPRECATED — conflated announced intent with measured reachability. Use lifecycle (curated) and availability (measured) instead. Retained so existing files validate; scripts/migrate-status.mjs converts.

lastChecked.description: Date of the last availability probe. Point-in-time only; the uptime record lives in status/ (see status.schema.json).

timeDimension.description: Declares that this layer's endpoint carries a time dimension, written as a {time} token in the tile template. Modelled on the OGC WMTS 1.0.0 <Dimension> element, whose UOM for this dimension is ISO8601; WMS-T (WMS 1.3.0 Annex C) uses the same ISO 8601 vocabulary for its TIME parameter. The consumer resolves {time} to a concrete ISO 8601 value before requesting tiles.

identifier.description: Dimension identifier as the service declares it. WMTS RESTful templates spell the token with this name, e.g. {Time}.

default.description: Value to use when the consumer has no time selected. Either the keyword 'latest' (resolve against the clock, honouring 'lag') or a fixed ISO 8601 instant. WMS-T spells this 'current'; that keyword is not used here because WMTS services advertise whether they support it and many, including NASA GIBS, do not.

extent.description: Validity, as ISO 8601 intervals in WMTS <Value> form: start/end/period, e.g. '2000-02-24/2026-09-05/P1D'. 'latest' is permitted as the end of an open interval.

period.description: ISO 8601 duration between successive values, e.g. P1D, P8D, P1M. The step for a time slider.

precision.description: How much of the ISO 8601 instant the endpoint expects. 'day' renders 2026-09-05; 'second' renders 2026-09-05T14:30:00Z.

coverage.description: Whether ONE instant covers the whole extent. 'partial' means a single time yields orbital swaths or otherwise incomplete cover (satellite L2 products), and no choice of time will fill it in — only a composited or analysed product does. Choosing a time is therefore not a way to get full cover; this field tells the user which products can offer it at all.

compositedOver.description: ISO 8601 duration the product is already composited over, when one instant represents an aggregate rather than a moment (NDVI 8-day = P8D, monthly average = P1M). This is the mechanism by which a gappy instrument becomes full-cover; absent for instantaneous products.

lag.description: ISO 8601 duration by which the newest available data trails the clock. 'latest' resolves to now minus this. Without it a near-real-time layer asks for a tile that has not been produced yet and 404s.

lifecycle.description: Operator-announced intent, curated by hand. stable = in normal service; beta = offered without commitment; deprecated = end-of-life announced but still served; retired = withdrawn. Never written by tooling.

availability.description: Last measured reachability, written by scripts/test-layers.mjs. up = 2xx; auth-required = 401/403, endpoint alive but rejected our credentials; down = 4xx/5xx other than auth; unreachable = DNS/TLS/timeout, no HTTP response; unknown = not testable (no config, or key missing). Never edited by hand.

operator.description: Who runs the service, as a durability signal. A national mapping agency and a hobby tile server are ranked differently even when they serve the same featuretype.

type.description: government = national/regional public body; intergovernmental = EU, UN, ESA and similar; commercial = company with paying customers; research = university or institute; community = volunteer project with governance (OSM, OpenTopoMap); individual = one person's server

name.description: Legal or institutional name, when it differs from provider.name

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the operating body

since.description: Year the service has been operating since, if known

sla.description: Only for a published, committed service level. Absence means no SLA, not an unknown one.

cost.description: What using this costs in practice. Richer successor to provider.access, which stays for back-compat. Belongs on a service once services are modelled — a provider can price two endpoints differently.

model.description: free = no account, no charge; freemium = free tier then metered; registration = free but account required; paid = charged from the first request

price.description: Metered price points beyond the free tier. Indicative, not a quote.

attributionRequired.description: Visible attribution is a licence condition

checked.description: When these terms were last read off the provider's own pricing page. Prices go stale silently.

cost.description: Only when this layer is priced differently from the provider default

status.description: DEPRECATED — see provider.status. Use lifecycle + availability.

lastChecked.description: Date of the last availability probe. Uptime history lives in status/.

webmapxConfig.description: Ready-to-use config for webmapx. Either styleUrl (full MapLibre style) or source+layer (addSource/addLayer).

type.description: When 'style', this is a CompositeStyleLayerConfig — webmapx fetches url and renders the full style. Omit for source+layer configs.

url.description: Remote MapLibre style JSON URL. Used when type='style'. May contain {key-<name>} placeholders. webmapx substitutes keys then fetches and renders the full composite style.

tiles.description: Tile URL templates. Beyond MapLibre's own tokens ({z}/{x}/{y}, {quadkey}, {ratio}, {prefix}, {bbox-epsg-3857}, {s}), a template may carry {time} (or {Time}) for a time-dimensioned service. MapLibre does not substitute {time} — the consumer must resolve it from the layer's time declaration before adding the source.
